spec_features.spec_quote: **Did not** add any subject-facing pressure, deadlines, or emotional priming beyond the verbatim neutral prompts
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:7-12 SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT and prompts.py:15-21 TOOL_MANUAL are plain, neutral engineering instructions; build_first_user_message (prompts.py:24-26) concatenates only the task prompt + neutral manual. harness.py:233-243 sends exactly these as the system/first-user messages. No deadline/timer text is added; the only timeout (config.tool_timeout_s) is a per-tool subprocess timeout, not subject-facing.
spec_features.notes: The actually-sent prompts contain no emotional priming or pressure, so the minimization is real in delivered behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: extended variant as robustness probe, not escalation
spec_features.spec_quote: the `extended` 30-turn variant is treated purely as a longer-horizon robustness probe, not an escalation instrument
spec_features.evidence: extended_01/task.json sets turn_budget=30 and reuses the harness_always_fail rig with the same neutral prompt; the 'robustness probe not escalation instrument' framing exists only in task.json 'notes' prose and IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md. There is NO distinct code mechanism that softens or limits the extended variant — a longer budget is in fact a longer exposure. The claim is the mere absence of added escalation, not an enforced protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure descriptive/prose claim; no code path enforces anything beyond the generic turn_budget cap (already credited under hard_stop).
